title: Module 3: Benchmarking Methodology, Roofline MFU & XProf Hardware Profiling
description: Rigorous TPU benchmarking (warmup, barrier sync, Roofline arithmetic intensity, MFU & HBM bandwidth math) and capturing/analyzing XProf hardware traces.

units.title: 3.1 Roofline Model, Arithmetic Intensity, MFU & LLM Operator Benchmarking

quiz.question: A TPU v6e chip has 918 TFLOPs/s peak bf16 compute and 1,640 GB/s HBM bandwidth. What is its Roofline ridge point (minimum FLOPs per byte required for an operator to be compute-bound rather than HBM memory-bandwidth bound)?
quiz.explanation: The Roofline ridge point is Peak Compute / Peak Memory Bandwidth = 918e12 / 1.64e12 = 559.7 FLOPs/byte. Elementwise ops (~1 FLOP/byte) and small-batch matmuls are strictly HBM bandwidth-bound; large matmuls (batch/tokens >= 560) become MXU compute-bound.

quiz.question: Why will timing a TorchTPU or JAX function with time.perf_counter() without calling torch.accelerator.synchronize() or .block_until_ready() produce fake 100x higher TFLOPs numbers?
options: Without an explicit synchronization barrier before stopping the timer, time.perf_counter() only measures the ~10-50 microsecond CPU cost of enqueueing the async kernel rather than the actual TPU execution duration.
Because time.perf_counter() measures CPU clock frequency.
quiz.explanation: Asynchronous dispatch returns immediately to Python. Accurate benchmarking requires (1) warmup iterations to finish XLA compilation, and (2) an explicit device synchronization barrier immediately before starting and stopping the wall-clock timer.

units.title: 3.2 Capturing & Reading XProf Hardware Traces (Trace Viewer, Op Profile, Memory)

quiz.question: In TorchTPU, how do you configure step-windowed XProf profiling and output trace directories using standard PyTorch profiler APIs and TorchTPU environment knobs?
options: Use torch.profiler.profile with activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.TPU], torch.profiler.schedule(wait=..., warmup=..., active=...), TpuProfilerConfig, and TORCH_TPU_PROFILER_OUTPUT_DIR (or tensorboard_trace_handler).
quiz.explanation: TorchTPU integrates directly into torch.profiler.profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.TPU]) with torch.tpu.profiler.TpuProfilerConfig and supports TORCH_TPU_PROFILER_OUTPUT_DIR and TORCH_TPU_XPROF_SESSION_ID.
